extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, judges, and law students studying equity remedies and defenses in U.S. patent litigation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when courts of equity will grant, continue, or dissolve injunctions in patent cases, and on related procedural and substantive requirements (parties, contents of the bill, affidavits, defenses, and statutory constructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surreptitious or unjust obtaining of a patent (fraud) as a complete defence
rubrics_metrics.description: That the patentee 'had surreptitiously or unjustly obtained the patent for that which was in fact invented or discovered by another, who was using reasonable diligence in adapting and perfecting the same.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a defence, if made out, is a complete bar to the action. One mode of surreptitious obtaining is acquiring knowledge of the invention from public records where the original inventor deposited a description. The jury may infer piracy from the existence of a prior record of which every subsequent patentee is presumed to have knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority between independent inventors & 'reasonable diligence' rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of two independent inventors, the earlier inventor who was 'using reasonable diligence in adapting and perfecting the same' may successfully defend, even if another later actually perfected and reduced the invention to practice first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The law favors the first inventor in point of time if the earlier inventor was exercising reasonable diligence. The section qualifies the right of the first person who actually perfected the invention by giving priority to an earlier inventor who was diligently adapting and perfecting the thing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-record notice presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: When a real inventor has filed a description at the patent office or obtained a patent, he has given notice to every subsequent applicant for the same thing, and a jury may infer piracy from the existence of that former record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is a presumption of law that a subsequent patentee has knowledge of preceding patents recorded in the patent office; courts may treat such records as putting later applicants on inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to practice / patentability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor 'who has first perfected and adapted the same to use' is the first inventor in the sense of the Act; 'an imperfect and incomplete invention, resting in mere theory ... and not actually reduced to practice, is not, and indeed cannot be, patentable under our patent acts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until an invention is perfected and adapted to practical use it is not patentable; in a race, he who first reduces it to a fixed, positive, and practical form is generally entitled to priority, subject to the reasonable-diligence qualification noted above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory bar for alien patentees failing to put invention on sale
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patentee, being an alien when the patent was granted, 'had failed and neglected for the space of eighteen months from the date of the patent, to put and continue on sale to the public, on reasonable terms, the invention or discovery,' this provision was intended to prevent foreign inventors from withholding use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision aims to prevent foreign patentees from obtaining patents and then unreasonably withholding the invention from public use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable grounds for granting injunctions in patent cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts of equity grant injunctions to prevent irreparable mischiefs, to suppress multiplicity of suits and vexatious litigation, and to enable more complete discovery of the extent of injury than would be available at law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent statutes direct courts to grant injunctions according to the course and principles of equity; injunctions complement legal damages when preventive relief is indispensable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion of the court in granting/interlocutory injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The court has large latitude and discretion in dealing with applications for interlocutory or final injunctions, subject to well-settled equitable rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlocutory options include: grant simpliciter; grant but direct plaintiff to establish title at law and suspend until result (defendant keeping an account); or refuse/dismiss. At hearing the court may in rare cases grant an injunction without recourse to a trial at law, depending on pleadings, conduct, nature of patent right, and strength of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be parties/complainants in equity for patent infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties entitled to equitable relief are the party or parties interested in the patent — patentee, assignees, or grantees of the exclusive right for a particular district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an assignee has the whole interest he may sue alone; if less than whole interest he must join the patentee. An unrecorded assignment may prevent the assignee from maintaining suit in equity or at law. Different persons who have infringed independently cannot be joined as defendants in the same bill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special treatment of grantees with exclusive district rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantee of the exclusive right for a specified portion of the United States may maintain an action at law in his own name within his district; in equity the patentee may be joined with such an assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In equity, an assignee who has a limited exclusive right (e.g., to use a limited number of machines in a district) may properly join the patentee because the patentee retains an interest (e.g., licensing further uses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of a bill for an injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill should recite the application for letters-patent, compliance with prerequisites, issue of letters (giving the title verbatim), attestation, and delivery to the patentee; profert of the letters should be made though specification need not be set forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bill must also state that the plaintiff put the invention into use and is in exclusive possession at filing; if based on assignment, renewal, extension, or disclaimer relevant facts must be set forth; must allege actual or threatened infringement; note prior actions/injunctions; state requests to defendants to desist; include charges of combination or conspiracy if relevant; and conclude with a prayer for discovery on oath, specific answers, an account of gains/profits, an injunction, delivery or destruction of infringing items, further relief, and process (writ, subpoena). The bill should be sworn to by affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of surrender and renewal of patent during injunction proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent is surrendered and renewed pending a temporary injunction, a supplemental bill is necessary to continue the injunction as to the new patent; courts have continued injunctions as to renewed patents where assignees consented to surrender/renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commissioner’s grant of a new patent for the same invention is prima facie binding in the equity-stage; the court will usually treat the new patent as covering the same invention for purposes of continuing an injunction unless clear excess of authority or collusion appears on the face of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of originality/belief of first invention when seeking injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain an injunction the plaintiff should accompany his application with an affidavit that he believes himself to be the original and first inventor of the thing patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances may arise after obtaining a patent that convince the patentee he was mistaken; judges have required such a special affidavit annexed to a bill, and it is usual on moving for an injunction before answer to read such affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement — no ex parte injunctions without notice in U.S. patent cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In the courts of the United States, notice that an injunction is to be applied for must be served on the defendant; no injunction, temporary or final, can be granted without reasonable previous notice to the adverse party or his attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus injunctions in patent cases are not granted ex parte; they may, however, be granted on filing the bill and before answer provided proper notice has been given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of 'use before application' under the Act of 1839
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of the invention before an application for a patent must be the specific improvement then invented and used by the person who had purchased, constructed, or used the machine to which the invention is applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This construction limits the defense of prior use to the particular improvement actually invented and used by the prior user, avoiding a literalism that would create confusion among earlier statutes and terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity relief may be sought quia timet (for apprehended infringement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill will lie for an injunction where the patent right is admitted or established upon well-grounded proof of an apprehended intention of the defendant to violate the patent right (quia timet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A previously granted injunction is prima facie evidence of intended violation; affidavits of intent or other strong evidence may support a quia timet bill even before an actual breach has occurred.
